service: CIPC — Companies and Intellectual Property Commission
overview: CIPC registers companies, co-operatives, and intellectual property (trademarks, patents, designs) in South Africa. If you want to start a formal business, you register it here.

services.name: Company Registration (Pty Ltd)
services.description: A private company (Proprietary Limited) is the most common business structure in South Africa.
requirements: At least one director who is a natural person (a real human, not another company)
A unique company name (check availability on the CIPC website)
A registered address in South Africa
A Memorandum of Incorporation (MOI) — CIPC provides a standard template
how_to_register: Step 1: Create an account on www.cipc.co.za
Step 2: Reserve your company name (R50) — takes 1-2 business days for approval
Step 3: Once the name is approved, complete the company registration (CoR 14.1 form)
Step 4: Upload your MOI (use the CIPC standard template or a custom one prepared by an attorney)
Step 5: Pay the registration fee (R175 for online)
Step 6: CIPC issues a Registration Certificate — usually within 1-3 business days
Step 7: Register for tax with SARS immediately after receiving your registration certificate

costs.total: R225 for a basic Pty Ltd registration

after_registration: Register for tax with SARS (Income Tax, VAT if applicable, PAYE if you have employees)
Register for UIF if you have employees
Register for Compensation Fund (COIDA) if you have employees
Open a business bank account (you will need your registration certificate)
File annual returns with CIPC (due every year on your registration anniversary)

services.name: Annual Returns
services.description: Every registered company MUST file an annual return with CIPC every year. Failure to do so can result in your company being deregistered.
services.when: Due every year on the anniversary month of your company's registration
services.cost: R450 for a private company (Pty Ltd)
how: Log in to the CIPC website
Confirm or update your company details
what_happens_if_you_miss_it: If you still don't file, CIPC begins the deregistration process
A deregistered company cannot trade, cannot enter contracts, and cannot sue or be sued
Re-registration is possible but costs approximately R700 and takes weeks

services.name: Director Amendments
services.description: When you add, remove, or change directors of your company.
how: Log in to CIPC and submit a CoR 39 form (change of directors)
Upload the new director's ID and consent letter

services.name: Company Name Change
how: Submit a special resolution signed by all shareholders
Submit CoR 9.4 form on the CIPC website
Update your MOI to reflect the new name

services.name: Close Corporation (CC) Conversion
services.description: Close Corporations (CCs) can no longer be registered, but existing CCs can continue to operate or convert to Pty Ltd companies.
how: Submit a CK2A form to convert from CC to Pty Ltd
Prepare a new MOI for the company
The CC registration number changes to a company registration number

services.name: Trademark Registration
services.description: Protect your brand name, logo, or slogan from being used by others.
process: Search the trademark database to check availability
File a trademark application on the CIPC website or through a trademark attorney
If approved, the trademark is published in the Patent Journal for opposition (3 months)
If no opposition, the trademark is registered — valid for 10 years, renewable
services.tip: Consider using a trademark attorney for complex applications — errors can result in rejection and you lose the fee

cipc_offices.name: CIPC Self-Service Terminal — Durban
cipc_offices.address: 267 Anton Lembede Street, Durban CBD (at the Department of Employment and Labour)
cipc_offices.note: Limited services available in person — most CIPC services are online only

online_portal.services: Company registration, annual returns, director changes, trademark applications, name reservations
online_portal.tip: The website can be slow. Use Chrome browser. Try early morning (before 08:00) for best performance.

common_problems.problem: CIPC website not working / constantly timing out
common_problems.what_to_do: This is a very common complaint. Try different browsers, try early morning, clear your cache. If persistent, call 086 100 2472. CIPC has acknowledged ongoing website performance issues.

common_problems.problem: Company deregistered for not filing annual returns
common_problems.what_to_do: Apply for re-registration on the CIPC website. Submit a CoR 40.5 form. Fee: R700. You will need to file all outstanding annual returns and pay all outstanding fees.

common_problems.problem: Someone registered a company using your identity
common_problems.what_to_do: Report immediately to CIPC and to SAPS. CIPC will investigate and can deregister the fraudulent company. Check your credit report for any business accounts opened in your name.
Download it from the CIPC website — log in and navigate to 'My Companies'. If it's not there, call 086 100 2472.

escalation.step_2: Email a formal complaint to info@cipc.co.za with all reference numbers
escalation.step_3: Escalate to the CIPC Commissioner's office
escalation.step_4: Lodge a complaint with the Department of Trade, Industry and Competition (DTIC)
escalation.legislation: Companies Act 71 of 2008, Intellectual Property Laws

your_rights: You have the right to register a company if you meet the requirements
CIPC must process applications within the published timeframes
You have the right to access the public company register
Your personal information held by CIPC is protected under POPIA
